Commercial scope (summary): be the initial estate administrator This agreement sets the rules for administering the late father’s estate. Bob Jones will serve as the initial estate administrator and will handle the estate in a practical, documented way. He may pay funeral bills and urgent property expenses first, then address other estate obligations in the proper order. He will keep receipts and provide monthly accounting updates so the family can track what has been paid, what remains outstanding, and what assets are still in the estate. Reasonable costs incurred in administering the estate may be reimbursed from estate funds. No distributions will be made until debts and taxes have been handled. Major assets may not be sold without majority written approval from the family members entitled to approve that decision. If Bob Jones resigns or can no longer serve, a replacement administrator will be appointed under the same family approval process. Family financial information and estate records will be kept confidential and shared only as needed for administration, reporting, tax, legal, or approval purposes.

The estate will reimburse the administrator for reasonable out-of-pocket costs incurred in administering the estate, including documented funeral bills and urgent property expenses paid on the estate’s behalf. Reimbursement is conditioned on receipts and supporting records. No beneficiary distributions will be made until estate debts and taxes have been satisfied.
